data.title: Eval harness: planted-fault fixture kind (data), scoring, miss-rate and enable-by-default verdict
Eval harness: standard fake kit (clock, agent, meters, control plane, hub, bench, vendor tool)
Eval harness: runner, miss-rate report surface and enable-by-default gate

data.body:
Twelve evaluation tasks and fifty acceptance tasks each build their own fixtures; one harness gives a fixture registry, a standard fake kit, a miss-rate report per workflow and the rule that a workflow is enabled by default only after it catches its planted set; extends the live-recorded fixtures (B-ac-fixtures).

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition this task adds (kind, template, gate, lens, role, lint set, importer, pack, job) is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12 (add, edit, remove as a tombstone, review and history, search, recall and RAG export, logged events and replay restore); every shipped default is overridable per project and per org; search for an existing function and extend the shared engines (P-shared-engines) instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB.

Split into: SE-eval-harness.1, SE-eval-harness.2, SE-eval-harness.3.

data.claim: A TOML evalfixture kind rides the generic record surface, and scoring by word match gives a deterministic miss rate
data.falsifier: the kind failing the shared add/show/edit/remove/search test, or the scorer giving different results on a rerun
data.mechanism: kinddata loads templates/kinds/*.toml; planted entries id=word|word are matched case-insensitively against finding text
data.probe_output: evalfixture passes the packaged-kind add/show/edit/remove cycle; scorer tests 6 passed
data.question: Can planted-fault fixtures be a TOML data kind with a pure word-match scorer, no second engine?

evidence.note: reuses core/kinddata TOML kinds and the generic record surface; no second engine; files <20KB

chunk_findings.detail:
The guard is documented and reported as counting *planted-fault* fixtures ("needs at least {min_fixtures} planted-fault fixture(s); has {row['fixtures']}"), but `report` fills `fixtures` with `len(rows)`, i.e. every `Score` recorded for the workflow — including clean fixtures that plant nothing. A fixture with `planted = []` yields a `Score` with `planted == 0`, `missed == 0`, and enters `by` just like any other, so it inflates the count that this check consumes.

Concrete failure: with `min_fixtures = 3`, a workflow evaluated on three fixtures where two have no `planted` entries and the third has a single planted fault that is caught produces `row["fixtures"] == 3 >= 3`, `miss_rate == 0.0`, and `enable_by_default` returns `(True, ...)` — the workflow is enabled by default although only one planted-fault fixture was ever exercised, which is exactly the evidence the reason string claims was required. A harness that adds clean fixtures (the kind this module explicitly models, see the "on a clean fixture, a false positive" note) can therefore push a thinly-tested workflow past the `min_fixtures` gate; the check should count fixtures with `s.planted > 0` (or the parameter should be compared against `sum(1 for s in rows if s.planted)`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/evalharness.py:enable_by_default (the `row["fixtures"] < min_fixtures` check)
